get.description: What a client needs to know at start-up: API version, server time, whether the platform is under maintenance, and which features are currently open. Public endpoint.

429.description: Too many requests or attempts (`RATE_LIMITED`); see the `Retry-After` header.

get.description: Every setting with the value in force. `isDefault` is true while no decision has been recorded: features are then closed. Requires `system_settings.read`.

429.description: Too many requests or attempts (`RATE_LIMITED`); see the `Retry-After` header.

put.description:
Opens or closes a feature (`features.*`, boolean value) or sets the maintenance mode (`maintenance.mode`). The change, its author and the mandatory `reason` are written to the audit log in the same transaction. Requires `system_settings.write`.

Opening a regulated feature is a business decision: technical availability is not a legal authorisation.

429.description: Too many requests or attempts (`RATE_LIMITED`); see the `Retry-After` header.

post.description: Creates an individual account and e-mails a 6-digit verification code. The account cannot sign in until the address is verified. Signing up again with an address whose sign-up was never completed replaces it entirely. The answer is the same whether or not an account exists for this address, so that the endpoint cannot be used to find out who has an account. Requires the `registration` feature to be open.

422.description: Understood but refused by a business rule (`UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY`, `COUNTRY_NOT_SUPPORTED`).

429.description: Too many requests or attempts (`RATE_LIMITED`); see the `Retry-After` header.

post.description: Confirms the address with the code received by e-mail **and the password chosen at sign-up**, and activates the account: only the person who both receives the code and chose the password can activate it. A code can be tried 5 times; a wrong code answers `INVALID_OR_EXPIRED_CODE`, whatever its cause. A right code with another password answers `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`: sign up again to replace the unfinished sign-up.

204.description: Address verified. The account can now sign in.

429.description: Too many requests or attempts (`RATE_LIMITED`); see the `Retry-After` header.

post.description: Replaces the previous code. At most 3 codes per account every 15 minutes. The answer is the same whether or not an account exists for this address, so that the endpoint cannot be used to find out who has an account.

429.description: Too many requests or attempts (`RATE_LIMITED`); see the `Retry-After` header.

post.description:
Opens a session and returns its tokens. Send the access token with every request (`Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`); use the refresh token to obtain a new pair before the access token expires.

**Read `status`.** `AUTHENTICATED`: the session is open. `MFA_REQUIRED`: the account is protected by two-step verification and no session is open yet — send `mfaToken` and a code to `POST /auth/mfa/verify` within 5 minutes.

Send a stable random `deviceId` (created once per installation): a sign-in from a device the account has never used is reported to its holder by e-mail.

A wrong e-mail or a wrong password both answer `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`. After 5 failures in 15 minutes the client is blocked for 15 minutes (`RATE_LIMITED`, see `Retry-After`). `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED` and `ACCOUNT_DISABLED` are only returned when the password is correct.

429.description: Too many requests or attempts (`RATE_LIMITED`); see the `Retry-After` header.

post.description:
Second step of a sign-in that answered `MFA_REQUIRED`: the `mfaToken`, and either the 6-digit `code` of the authenticator app or a `recoveryCode` (single use). Opens the session.

A code is accepted once. A wrong code answers `INVALID_OR_EXPIRED_CODE`; after 5 wrong codes the token is void (`UNAUTHENTICATED`: sign in again) and the second step of the account is blocked for 15 minutes (`RATE_LIMITED`).

429.description: Too many requests or attempts (`RATE_LIMITED`); see the `Retry-After` header.

post.summary: Complete a sign-in with the second step

post.description: Exchanges the refresh token for a new pair. **The refresh token changes at every call**: store the new one. Presenting a refresh token that was already used revokes the whole session (it means the token was copied), except within a few seconds of its use, to tolerate a lost response.

429.description: Too many requests or attempts (`RATE_LIMITED`); see the `Retry-After` header.

post.description: Replaces the password and **closes every session** of the account. Two-step verification, if enabled, stays in place. A code can be tried 5 times; every failure answers `INVALID_OR_EXPIRED_CODE`.

post.description:
Only an active account can be suspended. Its sessions are closed at once and it can no longer sign in (`ACCOUNT_DISABLED`). The holder is told by e-mail — never why — unless `notifyUser` is `false`. Requires `users.suspend`.

The mandatory `reason` is written to the audit log with the action. You cannot act on your own account, and acting on a staff account (one that holds a role) also requires `roles.manage`.

info.title: MG-Exchange API
info.description:
MG-Exchange platform API.

**Conventions**
- Versioned routes: `/api/v1/...`.
- Monetary amounts are decimal **strings** (`"12.34"`), never JSON numbers.
- Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC.
- Errors use `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457) with a stable `code` and the `requestId`.
- Every route requires `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` unless stated otherwise.
- Every response carries an `X-Request-Id` header for support and log correlation.
